basis.text: The corps bivouacked about 3 miles short on the night of 1 July (Hancock; Brooke 9.30 p.m.). Smyth's brigade was in position at 4 a.m. (Smyth, 17 Jul 1863), the corps was up before six (Haskell, a letter of July 1863) and 'up' at 6.15 (a dispatch from army headquarters); Webb was in position at 6.30. Hancock's own arrival 'about 7 a.m.' is later than all of these.

default.label: Window 04:00-06:15 on Jul 2: first brigades about 4, the main body up by 6; drawn at 06:00
default.basis_text: Lower bound: Smyth's brigade in position at 4 a.m. and Dent's regiment on the field about 4. Upper bound: the headquarters dispatch timed 6.15 a.m. (the Second Corps is up), which Haskell's letter (up to the field before six) puts at 06:00 or a little earlier. Webb's 6.30, Hancock's about 7 and the tail regiments' 8 to 10 are later moments.

animation.note: The corps' main body is drawn arriving by 06:00, the hour Haskell's letter gives as its upper bound ('before six'; the dispatch has it up by 6.15); the first brigades of the Third Division are drawn from 04:00 and the tail regiments (about 8 to 10) later, each by its own unit row. 04:00 is the earliest source-supported time for any part of the corps; nothing is drawn before it.

weighing.summary: The plan lists 22:30 on 1 July, 'at dawn', 06:00 and 07:00, and recommends 06:00 for the head with tails later. The record gives a march in stages. The night of 1 July the corps lay about 3 miles short (Hancock; Brooke's brigade there about 9.30 p.m.), so 22:30 on the ridge is contradicted. Smyth's brigade was in position at 4 a.m. and Dent's regiment on the field about then; the First Division's first brigade came up soon after sunrise; a dispatch from army headquarters at 6.15 has the Second Corps 'up'; Haskell, in the column, has it up to the field before six; Webb was put in position at 6.30; Hancock puts the arrival about 7; two regiments of Brooke's brigade give about 8 and about 10. The dispatch is the best class of writing and, with Haskell, makes 06:00 an upper bound for the main body; Hancock's about 7 is outweighed by the dispatch of 6.15 and the letter, which have the corps up earlier (he rode ahead and rejoined the corps on the road, so his hour may be his own arrival); Webb's 6.30 is a placement after the arrival. The first troops were earlier than the plan's 06:00 'head'. So the default is the window 04:00-06:15, drawn at 06:00.
weighing.who: Seth Williams wrote from army headquarters; Haskell rode with the corps on Gibbon's staff; Smyth, Webb and Brooke commanded brigades and give their own movements; Dent, Devereux, McMichael, Scherrer and Coates commanded or served in regiments; Hancock commanded the corps but rode on ahead on 1 July and rejoined it on the road. Meade gives an upper bound for the army.
weighing.when: The dispatch is of 2 July 6.15 a.m. (the sender's own time). Haskell wrote in July 1863; Smyth, McMichael and Webb in July; Devereux 7 Jul; Coates 3 Aug, Scherrer 2 Aug, Gibbon 7 Aug, Brooke 15 Aug; Hancock's report is of 1863 or 1864 (the year digit is damaged); Meade 1 Oct 1863.
weighing.where: Each brigade stood where it arrived: Smyth and Dent on the right near the Taneytown road, Brooke on the left of the Second Division, Webb on the ridge, Haskell by the Taneytown road, Hancock rejoining on the road. One corps arrives as several columns, so a unit's report dates a unit, not the corps.
weighing.how_knew: Smyth, Webb, Brooke, Devereux and Dent give their own movements; Haskell saw the column; Hancock's 'about 7' is his own arrival back at the corps, not a timed observation of the head; the dispatch is a timed record.
weighing.clock: All the witnesses are Union and no correction is applied (the plan's note of about 20 minutes between the armies' clocks plays no part here). 'About 4' and 'about 7' are read as plus or minus a quarter hour; 'before six' is an upper bound.
weighing.independence: Smyth and Dent are one brigade (the lower bound rests on one brigade, flagged as such where it stands alone). Haskell and the dispatch are two independent records for the upper bound. Brooke, McMichael and Scherrer are one brigade giving three hours. Hancock and Meade are separate; Meade's 'by 7' relays reports. Gibbon, Caldwell and Harrow give no hour.

source_panel_text: The Second Corps came up in stages on Jul 2: its first brigades about 04:00, the main body up before six (Haskell's letter; a headquarters dispatch at 6.15 has it up), the last regiments about 8 to 10. Hancock's own about 07:00 is later. The plan's 22:30 on Jul 1 is contradicted: the corps lay three miles short. Eleven other values are listed.

pdf_default.note: 06:00 holds as the hour by which the main body was up (the upper end of the window) and the tails were later; as the head of the column it is two hours late, since a brigade was in position at 4 a.m.

first_delegated.note: The window 06:30-07:00 dates a brigade's placement (Webb, 6.30) and Hancock's own arrival (about 7); a dispatch of 6.15 and a letter of the time have the corps up by then. It stays selectable. 22:30 contradicted, 06:00 and dawn stated only as unit moments, as the first pass found.
